title: cats1: policy, config and kit
summary: etc/cats1.policy turns Tom's standing rule into deny lines for every principal: Firewall, Keys, Forwarder, Host reboot, and run:nft iptables ssh-keygen systemctl reboot shutdown. Xtpd is denied until Tom adds an allow line (allow codex Xtpd bringup /etc/xtpd/xtpd.conf). Codex may submit jobs and remove files in /var/lib/newshell/work, nothing else. etc/agent.conf provides mu, net, svc, xtpd, host and ws. The cats contract forbids build tools on cats1, so the compile chain is a demonstration elsewhere, not a cats1 job. Kit: newshell-kit-v0.1-dev6-jammy.tar.gz (sha256 64e3edc6d3b8bfc73398e2fc9073bb8adc4de997188b81e9ee084a6eb07be120), built in the jammy chroot. Installed on cats1 with Tom's approval and proven there by Codex (REQ-00005621, 24 Nov): KIT_OK, self-test PASS with real readings (xtp_peers elementCount 3; audit thin 1, findingCount 0, invokerOnly 1, INVOKER sudo), nothing left running, post-test audit THIN. dev6 fixed what dev5 found on cats1: the audit counted its own sudo caller (now INVOKER), and the wrapped third xtp_peers element was lost. The mu-tools dev3 audit (programs and files, packages/mu_tools_v0.1-dev3) is separate; newshell's MuAuditor still uses the dev2 checks.
